flashcard_questions.q: What is a double circulatory system?
flashcard_questions.a: One in which blood passes through the heart twice on each complete circuit of the body.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than that of the right?
flashcard_questions.a: It must pump blood at high pressure all the way around the body.

flashcard_questions.q: Which vessel carries oxygenated blood away from the left ventricle?
Which vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the body into the right atrium?
Which vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs?
Which vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs into the left atrium?
Which arteries branch off the aorta to supply the heart muscle itself?

flashcard_questions.a: To stop blood flowing backwards as it returns to the heart at low pressure.

flashcard_questions.q: How thick are the walls of a capillary?
What is plasma, and what does it do?
flashcard_questions.a: The straw-coloured liquid of the blood, which transports dissolved substances around the body.

flashcard_questions.q: Which protein in red blood cells binds with oxygen in the lungs?
What is the role of platelets in the blood?
flashcard_questions.a: They help blood to clot at a wound by forming a mesh of fibrin threads.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to the coronary arteries in coronary heart disease?
flashcard_questions.a: Fatty material builds up inside them, narrowing them and reducing blood flow.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a stent treat coronary heart disease?
flashcard_questions.a: A small mesh tube holds the narrowed artery open, restoring normal blood flow.

flashcard_questions.q: How do statins slow the progress of coronary heart disease?
flashcard_questions.a: They lower blood cholesterol, slowing the rate at which fatty deposits build up.
